title: Rabbi Yosi Barʾ
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned under this name in [Yerushalmi Berakhot, chapter 8, halakhah 1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.8.1.5), where he says: ‘They are accustomed there, in a place where there is no wine,’ etc. The saying is cited in [Tosafot, Pesachim 106b](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Pesachim.106b), in the comment beginning ‘Mekadesh,’ where the name is Rabbi Yosi son of Rabbi Bun. Hyman holds that the earlier abbreviation was undoubtedly בר״ב, meaning ‘son of Rabbi Bun’; the bet subsequently dropped out, leaving בר׳. He is likewise mentioned by this name in Demai, chapter 2, at the end of halakhah 1.[^1]

notes.text: The earlier supplied transcription has ובגל״ס. The native page (PDF 320, printed 737) reads ובל״ס, the ordinary abbreviation for ובלי ספק, ‘and without doubt.’ Thus no otherwise unknown textual witness is asserted here: these are Hyman’s words of confidence in his reconstruction. The heading’s shortened בר׳ is retained as Barʾ because it is the form his notice explains. The named Vilna edition of [Tosafot, Pesachim 106b, s.v. Mekadesh arifta](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Pesachim.106b) explicitly gives רבי יוסי ב״ר בון in the no-wine passage, whereas the named Guggenheimer Hebrew edition of [Yerushalmi Berakhot 8:1:5](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Berakhot.8.1.5) reads רבי יוסי בריבי. These attestations support the cited contrast but do not prove Hyman’s proposed history of the lost bet. His ברכה is rendered by the work’s standard title, Berakhot. סה״א is rendered contextually as the end of halakhah 1; the Demai passage has not been independently checked.
